text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Lennart Meri appointed Mart Siimann as prime minister's candidate. Both a minority government and broadening the ruling coalition would be discussed at the negotiations, Siimann said.
- Visa-free travel between Estonia and Norway will come into force on May 1, experts of two foreign ministries agreed at a meeting in Tallinn.
- Meri left yesterday for a working visit to Sweden and will meet prime minister Goran Persson today.
- Security Police arrested an officer from Narva police Alexander Kompanijets, suspected in abusing power and violence towards policemen.
- Trial over barrister Monika Magi, charged with attempting to bribe a judge with 10,000 kroons, will be closed for the public, a court decided yesterday.
- A new road between Tallinn and key southern town Tartu will be built more modestly than initially planned, with a speed limit of 120 kilometres per hour instead of 140.
- Estonian and Finnish interior ministries signed a protocol on joint cooperation projects and a plan to hold regular meetings twice a year.
- The National Library in Tallinn registered its 100,000th reader yesterday.

- The Tax Department has lost a court case, started by a taxpayer who demanded back income tax he had paid for shares, bought for privatisation vouchers. If the State Court does not overrule the court decision, thousands of people would be in a position to demand back their income tax.
